referents.why: Plural 'to them' is the crowd that the chief priests stirred up and to whom Barabbas is to be released. The noun crowd is a singular collective and takes a plural pronoun by sense.
The one who releases a prisoner is Pilate, the releaser of 15:6 and 15:9. Barabbas is the object released, so the builder's referent makes the released man the releaser, which the act rules out.

links.why: Greek hina with the subjunctive: the stirring up is done so that the release happens. This is what the action is for.
Self link. No fused waw joins this clause to an earlier one within the verse.

none_fit.what: A verse-opening 'but' contrasting the chief priests' action with Pilate's offer in 15:9-10 has no host in its verse, so the contrast type cannot record it. Left unlinked.
